correctness.rationale: Finite-dimensional dissipative spectral argument proves the infinite-time limit equals the orthogonal projection onto common H-eigenvectors annihilated by both positive sinks. Fourier diagonalization shows degeneracy only at 0 and 1/2 flux. Explicit normalized sine vectors give the two exact absorber-divisibility conditions; finite root-of-unity sums evaluate every site probability and dark dimension, with trace giving the uniform-source average. No asymptotic or computational gap is needed. Independent matrix eigenprojectors and late-time non-Hermitian exponentials were checked in 825 and 7 parameter settings, respectively, including unequal rates; numerical tests are corroboration only.
